subject.title: feat(agents/mcp): scope MCP servers per-agent via generic agents allowlist [AI-assisted]

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core top-level `mcp.servers.*.agents` exact-id, fail-closed allowlist for all runtimes after the current code blockers are fixed?
rationale: The code shape is plausible, but the field decides which agents receive potentially credentialed MCP servers before later tool filtering, so exact-id, glob, subagent, unknown-agent, and fail-closed semantics need maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve exact-id allowlist after repairs
options.body: Fix the current fallback leak, summary/cache omission, and docs gap, then keep the additive exact-id fail-closed contract as the first core implementation.

options.title: Pause for broader scope semantics
options.body: Keep the draft paused while maintainers decide glob matching, subagent inheritance, unknown-agent doctor behavior, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Decline the core field
options.body: Close or redirect this PR if maintainers want MCP server scoping to live in a different API, plugin, or operator-policy surface.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-id allowlist after repairs
recommendation.body: Fix the current fallback leak, summary/cache omission, and docs gap, then keep the additive exact-id fail-closed contract as the first core implementation.
